name: Sine map
about: The map x → a sin(πx), a smooth one-hump map that follows the same period-doubling route to chaos as the logistic map.

name: Cubic map
about: The map x → a x(1 − x²), a symmetric map with two humps, so orbits can wander between positive and negative values.

name: Chebyshev map

name: Baker's map
about: A piecewise-linear map of the unit square that stretches it, cuts it in two and stacks the halves, like kneading dough: the textbook example of mixing.

name: Bedhead map
about: A two-dimensional trigonometric map from Ivan Emrich's collection of fractal-art attractors.

name: Blinking vortex map
about: Aref's blinking vortex sampled once per period: a fluid particle stirred by two point vortices that switch on and off in turn, the original model of chaotic advection (Aref 1984).

name: Bogdanov map
about: A planar map obtained by discretizing the Bogdanov–Takens normal form, with a Hopf bifurcation, mode locking and chaos (Bogdanov 1981; Arrowsmith et al. 1993).

name: Chirikov standard map
about: The kicked rotor, a pendulum kicked periodically: its phase space mixes regular islands (KAM tori) with chaos, a basic model of Hamiltonian chaos (Chirikov 1979).

name: De Jong map
about: A two-dimensional map built from sines and cosines, popularized by Peter de Jong as a source of fractal-art attractors.

name: Gauss map
about: The Gaussian (or 'mouse') map, x → e^{−a x²} + b: a bell-shaped one-hump map with period doubling, chaos and bistability.

name: Hénon map
about: Hénon's two-dimensional quadratic map, a simplified model of a Poincaré section of the Lorenz flow and the classic strange attractor of a map (Hénon 1976).

name: Hopalong map
about: Barry Martin's 'hopalong' map, built from a square root and an absolute value, popularized as a source of fractal art (Dewdney 1986).

name: Ikeda map
about: Light circulating in an optical ring cavity that contains a nonlinear medium, sampled once per round trip (Ikeda 1979).

name: Kaplan–Yorke map
about: A fully chaotic doubling map driving a contracting second variable, built to test the Kaplan–Yorke relation between Lyapunov exponents and fractal dimension (Kaplan & Yorke 1979).

name: Logistic map
about: May's discrete-time population model x → r x(1 − x), the textbook route to chaos through period doubling (May 1976).

name: Maynard Smith map
about: A second-order population model with delayed density dependence, x_{n+1} = y_n, y_{n+1} = a y_n + b − x_n² (Maynard Smith 1968).

name: Pickover map
about: A two-dimensional trigonometric map from Clifford Pickover's collection of fractal-art attractors.

name: Ricker map
about: Ricker's stock–recruitment model for fish, x → x e^{r(1 − x)}, in which overcompensating density dependence makes populations chaotic (Ricker 1954).

name: Svensson map
about: A two-dimensional trigonometric map from the collection of fractal-art attractors.

name: Lozi map
about: A piecewise-linear version of the Hénon map, with |x| in place of x², whose strange attractor can be analyzed exactly (Lozi 1978).

name: Arnold's cat map
about: A linear map of the torus that stretches and folds any picture (famously, a cat) into apparent noise: uniformly hyperbolic, fully chaotic and mixing (Arnold & Avez 1968).

name: Burgers map
about: A two-dimensional quadratic map, the discretized form of a pair of equations Burgers used as a toy model of turbulence (Whitehead & MacDonald 1984).

name: Coupled logistic maps
about: Two chaotic logistic maps, each nudged toward the other's state, so the pair moves between independent chaos and synchronization.

name: Chirikov standard map
about: The kicked rotor, a pendulum kicked periodically: its phase space mixes regular islands (KAM tori) with chaos, a basic model of Hamiltonian chaos (Chirikov 1979).

name: Aizawa system
about: A three-dimensional flow whose attractor winds around a sphere-like surface with a tube along its axis (Aizawa & Uezu 1982).

lines: \dot{x} &= - b x - d y + x z
\dot{y} &= - b y + d x + y z

name: Anishchenko–Astakhov oscillator
about: An electronic generator with inertial nonlinearity: amplification depends on a slowly heating element, which turns self-oscillation into chaos (Anishchenko & Astakhov).

name: Arneodo system
about: A jerk-type flow from Arneodo, Coullet and Tresser's study of strange attractors in Volterra-type equations, a classic example of Shilnikov chaos (Arneodo, Coullet & Tresser 1981).

lines: \dot{z} &= - a x - b y - c z + d x^{3}

name: Arnold–Beltrami–Childress flow
about: A steady, exact solution of Euler's equations for an inviscid 3-D fluid whose streamlines are chaotic; the series follows one fluid particle (Arnold 1965).

name: Arnold web
about: A nearly integrable Hamiltonian system, in which overlapping resonances form a web along which orbits drift slowly (Arnold diffusion) (Froeschlé, Guzzo & Lega 2000).

name: Atmospheric regime model
about: A low-order model of an atmospheric flow switching between regimes, built from coupled oscillators with widely separated frequencies (Tuwankotta 2006).

lines: \dot{y} &= \alpha y z + \beta z^{2} + \mu_{2} y + \omega z - \sigma x^{2}

name: Beer RNN
about: A small continuous-time recurrent neural network, of the kind used as a minimal model nervous system for simulated agents (Beer 1995).

name: Belousov–Zhabotinsky reaction
about: A three-variable model of the Belousov–Zhabotinsky reaction, an oscillating chemical reaction, in a regime with period doubling and chaos (Györgyi & Field 1992).

name: Bickley jet
about: A tracer in a model of a meandering atmospheric zonal jet flanked by vortices: a steady flow plus a time-periodic perturbation (Rypina et al. 2007).

name: Blasius system
about: A food chain of vegetation, herbivores and predators whose population peaks vary chaotically while their timing stays regular, as in the Canadian lynx cycle (Blasius, Huppert & Stone 1999).

lines: \dot{y} &= \frac{\alpha_{1} x y}{k_{1} x + 1} - \frac{\alpha_{2} y z}{k_{2} y + 1} - b y

name: Blinking rotlet
about: Viscous (Stokes) flow in a disk stirred by a point rotor that switches between two positions, a model of chaotic mixing (Meleshko & Aref 1996).

name: Blinking vortex
about: A fluid particle stirred by two point vortices that switch on and off in turn, the original model of chaotic advection (Aref 1984).

name: Bouali system
about: A model of economic cycles: a van der Pol-type oscillator extended with a feedback loop that represents fluctuating demand (Bouali 1999).

lines: \dot{x} &= - a x y + a x y_{0} - b z

name: Bouali system 2
about: A second variant of Bouali's economic-cycle model, an extended van der Pol-type oscillator with feedback (Bouali 1999).

lines: \dot{x} &= - a x y + a x y_{0} - b z
\dot{z} &= \mathrm{bb} m x z - c z - 1.5 m x

name: Burke–Shaw system
about: A three-dimensional flow related to the Lorenz system, with a scroll attractor symmetric about the z axis (Shaw 1981).

name: Calcium oscillator
about: Intracellular calcium oscillations driven by calcium-induced calcium release and IP₃ metabolism, here in a chaotic regime (Houart, Dupont & Goldbeter 1999).

name: Quasi-periodic calcium oscillator
about: The same intracellular calcium model at parameters that give quasi-periodic (torus) oscillations rather than chaos (Houart, Dupont & Goldbeter 1999).

name: Cellular neural network
about: A small cellular neural network: a few locally coupled analog neurons with piecewise-linear outputs, as built in hardware (Arena et al. 1998).

name: Chen system
about: A Lorenz-like system found by chaos anti-control (feedback designed to make a system chaotic), whose double-scroll attractor is not equivalent to Lorenz's (Chen & Ueta 1999).

lines: \dot{y} &= c y - x z + x \left(- a + c\right)

name: Chen–Lee system
about: A rigid body (a gyro) rotating under feedback control chosen to make its motion chaotic (Chen & Lee 2004).

name: Chua circuit
about: An electronic circuit of two capacitors, an inductor and a nonlinear negative resistor (Chua's diode), with the famous double-scroll attractor (Matsumoto 1984).

lines: \dot{x} &= \alpha \left(- m_{1} x - x + y - \left(0.5 m_{0} - 0.5 m_{1}\right) \left(- \left|{x - 1}\right| + \left|{x + 1}\right|\right)\right)

name: Circadian rhythm
about: A model of the Drosophila circadian clock (the PER and TIM proteins) driven by a light–dark cycle, which can respond chaotically (Leloup, Gonze & Goldbeter 1999).

name: Coevolving predator–prey
about: Predator–prey dynamics in which the prey's defensive trait evolves in response to the predator, which makes the populations fluctuate chaotically (Gilpin & Feldman 2017).

name: Colpitts system
about: The Colpitts oscillator, a single-transistor circuit used as a signal generator, which becomes chaotic for suitable component values (Kennedy 1994).

name: Coullet system
about: A jerk-type variant of the Arneodo system with a cubic nonlinearity (Arneodo, Coullet & Tresser 1981).

lines: \dot{z} &= - a x - b y - c z + d x^{3}

name: Dadras system
about: A three-dimensional quadratic flow that can generate two-, three- and four-scroll attractors depending on its parameters (Dadras & Momeni 2009).

lines: \dot{x} &= o y z - p x + y

name: Dequan Li system
about: A three-scroll chaotic attractor, one of the three-scroll unified chaotic systems (TSUCS) (Li 2008).

lines: \dot{x} &= - a x + a y + d x z
\dot{y} &= f y + k x - x z

name: Double gyre
about: A fluid particle in two counter-rotating gyres whose dividing line oscillates, a standard model for Lagrangian coherent structures in ocean flows (Shadden, Lekien & Marsden 2005).

name: Double pendulum
about: Two pendulums hung end to end, without friction: a conservative Hamiltonian system that is chaotic at high enough energy.

name: Excitable cell
about: A three-variable Hodgkin–Huxley-type model of an excitable cell membrane, whose bursts of spikes become chaotic (Chay 1985).

name: Finance model
about: A model of a financial system in which the interest rate, investment demand and price index interact nonlinearly (Cai & Huang 2007).

name: Fluid trampoline
about: A droplet bouncing on a vibrating soap film, which acts as a trampoline; at strong forcing the bounces become chaotic (Gilet & Bush 2009).

name: Forced Brusselator
about: Prigogine's Brusselator, a model autocatalytic chemical oscillator, driven periodically so that it can respond chaotically (Prigogine & Lefever 1968).

name: Forced FitzHugh–Nagumo
about: The FitzHugh–Nagumo neuron model driven by a periodic current, which gives irregular spiking (FitzHugh 1961).

name: Forced van der Pol
about: Van der Pol's triode oscillator with sinusoidal forcing, which can lock to the drive or respond chaotically (van der Pol 1920).

name: Genesio–Tesi system
about: A jerk-type flow (a third-order equation) with a single quadratic nonlinearity, from studies of chaos in feedback control systems (Genesio & Tesi 1992).

lines: \dot{z} &= - a z - b y - c x + x^{2}

name: Glycolytic oscillation
about: A model of glycolysis in which allosteric feedback on the enzymes (Monod–Wyman–Changeux kinetics) produces oscillations, including chaotic ones (Decroly & Goldbeter 1982).

name: Guckenheimer–Holmes system
about: A three-dimensional nonlinear oscillator, a rotating oscillation coupled to a third variable, from Guckenheimer and Holmes' study of nonlinear oscillations and bifurcations (Guckenheimer & Holmes 1983).

name: Hadley circulation
about: Lorenz's low-order model of the overturning Hadley cell of the atmosphere: a westerly jet exchanging energy with traveling eddies (the Lorenz-84 equations at different parameters) (Lorenz 1984).

name: Halvorsen system
about: A cyclically symmetric quadratic flow (x, y and z play identical roles in turn), one of Sprott's algebraically simple chaotic flows (Sprott 2010).

name: Hastings–Powell food chain
about: A three-species food chain (resource, consumer, predator) with saturating feeding, which produces the 'teacup' chaotic attractor (Hastings & Powell 1991).

name: Hénon–Heiles system
about: A star's motion in the mean gravitational potential of a galaxy, reduced to two degrees of freedom: a conservative system with both regular and chaotic orbits (Hénon & Heiles 1964).

name: Hindmarsh–Rose neuron
about: A three-variable neuron model with fast spiking and a slow adaptation current, which gives bursts of spikes that can be chaotic (Hindmarsh & Rose 1984).

lines: \dot{y} &= - a x^{3} - x^{2} \left(- b + d\right) + z

name: Hopfield network
about: A small continuous-time neural network with frustrated (mutually inconsistent) connections, which keep it from settling and make it chaotic (Lewis & Glass 1992).

name: Hyperchaotic Bao system
about: A four-dimensional hyperchaotic system (two positive Lyapunov exponents), obtained by adding a feedback variable to the Lü system (Bao & Liu 2008).

name: Hyperchaotic Cai system
about: A four-dimensional hyperchaotic extension of the Cai–Huang finance model (Cai & Huang 2007).

lines: \dot{y} &= b x + c y + w - x z

name: Hyperchaotic Jha system
about: A four-dimensional hyperchaotic system, with two positive Lyapunov exponents.

name: Hyperchaotic Lorenz system
about: A four-dimensional extension of the Lorenz system with an extra feedback variable, which makes it hyperchaotic (two positive Lyapunov exponents).

name: Hyperchaotic Lü system
about: A four-dimensional hyperchaotic system obtained from the Lü system by state-feedback control (Chen, Lu, Lü & Yu 2006).

name: Hyperchaotic Pang system
about: A four-dimensional hyperchaotic system derived from the Lü system (Pang & Liu 2011).

name: Hyperchaotic Qi system
about: A four-dimensional hyperchaotic variant of the Qi system (Qi, van Wyk, van Wyk & Chen 2008).

name: Hyperchaotic Wang system
about: A four-dimensional hyperchaotic extension of the Wang four-wing system (Wang et al. 2009).

name: Hyperchaotic Xu system
about: A four-dimensional hyperchaotic system, with two positive Lyapunov exponents.

name: Hyperchaotic Yan system

name: Hyperchaotic Yang–Chen system
about: A four-dimensional hyperchaotic system, with two positive Lyapunov exponents.

name: Interior squirmer
about: Slow viscous flow inside a cylinder driven by a time-periodic slip velocity at its wall, like the flow inside a swimming microorganism; a tracer in it moves chaotically (Blake 1971).

name: Isothermal chemical reaction
about: A model of an isothermal autocatalytic reaction with mixed-mode oscillations, in which large and small peaks alternate (Petrov, Scott & Showalter 1992).

name: Itik–Banks tumor model
about: Competing populations of tumor cells, healthy host cells and immune effector cells, whose interactions can be chaotic (Itik & Banks 2010).

lines: \dot{x} &= - a_{12} x y - a_{13} x z + x \left(1 - x\right)

name: Jerk circuit
about: An electronic circuit that implements a jerk equation (third-order), with a diode as its only nonlinearity (Sprott 2011).

name: Kawczynski–Strizhak reaction
about: A three-variable model of the Belousov–Zhabotinsky reaction that shows mixed-mode and chaotic oscillations (Strizhak & Kawczynski 1995).

name: Laser model
about: A three-dimensional model of a semiconductor laser, also realized as an electronic circuit (Abooee, Yaghini-Bonabi & Jahed-Motlagh 2013).

lines: \dot{x} &= - a x + a y + b y z^{2}

name: Lid-driven cavity flow
about: A fluid particle in a cavity whose two walls slide alternately, a model of chaotic mixing in a viscous flow (Grover et al. 2012).

name: Liu–Chen system
about: A three-dimensional chaotic flow with quadratic nonlinearities, proposed as a new member of the Lorenz–Chen family of attractors (Liu & Chen 2004).

lines: \dot{x} &= a x + h y + s y z
\dot{y} &= - b y - p x + q x z

name: Lorenz system
about: Lorenz's three-mode model of convection in a fluid layer heated from below, the original strange attractor, with its butterfly-shaped double lobe (Lorenz 1963).

name: Lorenz-84 system
about: Lorenz's low-order model of the general circulation of the atmosphere: a westerly jet exchanging energy with traveling eddies (Lorenz 1984).

lines: \dot{y} &= - b x z + g + x y - y
\dot{z} &= b x y + x z - z

name: Lorenz-96 system
about: Lorenz's model of an atmospheric quantity at equally spaced sites around a latitude circle, with advection, damping and constant forcing; the series is one site (Lorenz 1996).

name: Bounded Lorenz system
about: The Lorenz system modified by a confining term that keeps its orbits within a sphere (Sprott & Xiong 2015).

lines: \dot{x} &= - \sigma x + \sigma y + \frac{\sigma x^{3}}{r^{2}} - \frac{\sigma x^{2} y}{r^{2}} + \frac{\sigma x y^{2}}{r^{2}} + \frac{\sigma x z^{2}}{r^{2}} - \frac{\sigma y^{3}}{r^{2}} - \frac{\sigma y z^{2}}{r^{2}}

name: Coupled Lorenz system
about: Two Lorenz systems with different parameters, the second driven by the first through a coupling term, so their chaotic motions interact.

name: Lorenz–Stenflo system
about: A four-variable extension of the Lorenz system for acoustic-gravity waves in a rotating atmosphere, which can be hyperchaotic (Stenflo 1996).

lines: \dot{x} &= - a x + a y + d w

name: Lü–Chen system
about: A unified system that bridges the Lorenz and Chen attractors as one parameter varies (Lü & Chen 2002).

name: Lü–Chen–Cheng system
about: A Lorenz-like system that generates a four-scroll attractor (Lü, Chen & Cheng 2004).

lines: \dot{x} &= - \frac{a b x}{a + b} + c - y z

name: MacArthur consumer–resource model
about: Several plankton species competing for a few nutrients (MacArthur's consumer–resource model), whose abundances fluctuate chaotically (Huisman & Weissing 1999).

name: Moore–Spiegel oscillator
about: A fluid element oscillating in a temperature-stratified layer, a model from stellar convection (Moore & Spiegel 1966).

lines: \dot{z} &= \varepsilon y - b x - x^{2} y - z

name: Multi-scroll Chua circuit
about: A Chua-type circuit whose nonlinearity has several segments, so its attractor has several scrolls rather than two (Yalçın, Suykens & Vandewalle).

name: Newton–Leipnik system
about: Euler's equations for a rotating rigid body with linear feedback, which has two coexisting strange attractors (Leipnik & Newton 1981).

name: Nosé–Hoover oscillator
about: A particle in a harmonic potential coupled to a thermostat variable that holds its temperature fixed, a conservative system from molecular dynamics (Nosé 1984; Hoover 1985).

name: Nuclear quadrupole
about: A Hamiltonian model of collective quadrupole vibrations of an atomic nucleus, chaotic through overlapping resonances (Baran & Raduta 1998).

name: Oscillating flow
about: A fluid particle in a chain of convection rolls whose boundaries oscillate, a model of transport between rolls (Solomon & Gollub 1988).

name: Pan–Xu–Zhou system
about: A three-dimensional quadratic flow related to the Dequan Li attractor (Zhou et al. 2008).

lines: \dot{x} &= - a x + a y + d x z
\dot{y} &= f y + k x - x z

name: Pehlivan–Wei system
about: A three-dimensional quadratic flow with Hopf bifurcations of codimension one and two, also realized as an electronic circuit (Pehlivan & Wei 2012).

name: Qi system
about: A four-dimensional quadratic flow that is hyperchaotic (two positive Lyapunov exponents), with an unusually broad power spectrum (Qi, van Wyk, van Wyk & Chen 2008).

lines: \dot{x} &= - a x + a y + w y z
\dot{y} &= b x + b y - w x z

name: Qi–Chen system
about: A three-dimensional quadratic flow with a double-wing attractor, formed from two bistable attractors (Qi et al. 2008).

lines: \dot{x} &= - a x + a y + y z

name: Rabinovich–Fabrikant system
about: A model of the self-modulation of waves in a nonequilibrium medium such as a plasma, known for its unusually shaped attractors (Rabinovich & Fabrikant 1979).

lines: \dot{x} &= g x + x^{2} y + y z - y
\dot{y} &= g y - x^{3} + 3 x z + x

name: Rayleigh–Bénard convection
about: A low-order model of Rayleigh–Bénard convection, a fluid layer heated from below (Yanagita & Kaneko 1995).

name: Rikitake dynamo
about: Two coupled disk dynamos, a model of the irregular reversals of Earth's magnetic field (Rikitake 1958).

name: Rössler system
about: Rössler's minimal chaotic flow, with a single quadratic term: orbits spiral outward in a plane and are folded back in (Rössler 1976).

name: Rucklidge system
about: A model of double convection, in which temperature and a second quantity (such as salinity or a magnetic field) both drive the flow (Rucklidge 1992).

lines: \dot{x} &= - a x + b y - y z

name: Sakarya system
about: A three-dimensional flow whose four-wing attractor forms when two coexisting attractors merge (Li et al. 2015).

lines: \dot{x} &= a x + h y + s y z
\dot{y} &= - b y - p x + q x z

name: Salton Sea ecosystem
about: An eco-epidemiological model of the Salton Sea, California: healthy fish, infected fish and the fish-eating birds that prey on them (Upadhyay et al. 2007).

lines: \dot{y} &= \lambda x y - \frac{m y z}{a + y} - \mu y

name: San-Um–Srisuchinwong system
about: A flow with an absolute-value (piecewise) nonlinearity and a two-scroll attractor (San-Um & Srisuchinwong 2012).

name: Shimizu–Morioka system
about: A Lorenz-like model in which a symmetric limit cycle splits into asymmetric ones on the way to chaos (Shimizu & Morioka 1980).

name: Sprott A
about: Sprott's case A, the first of 19 algebraically simple chaotic flows (A–S) found by computer search. It has five terms and two quadratic nonlinearities and is conservative: a special case of the Nosé–Hoover oscillator (Sprott 1994).

name: Sprott B

name: Stick-slip oscillator
about: A weakly forced oscillator with dry friction, whose motion alternates between sticking and slipping (Awrejcewicz & Holicke 1999).

name: Swinging Atwood machine
about: Atwood's machine with one weight free to swing like a pendulum: a conservative system that is chaotic for some mass ratios (Tufillaro, Abbott & Griffiths 1984).

name: Thomas system
about: Thomas' cyclically symmetric attractor, ẋ = b sin y − a x and its cyclic permutations: a particle moving with friction through a 3-D lattice of forces (Thomas 1999).

name: Thomas labyrinth
about: Thomas' cyclically symmetric system at weak friction, whose orbits wander through a 3-D lattice of cells like a deterministic random walk (Thomas 1999).

name: Torus flow
about: A minimal quasi-periodic flow on a torus: two incommensurate rotations, so it never repeats, but it is not chaotic.

name: TSUCS2 system
about: The second form of the three-scroll unified chaotic system (TSUCS), related to the Dequan Li attractor (Pan, Zhou & Li 2013).

name: Vallis El Niño model
about: Vallis' three-variable model of El Niño: an ocean current and the east–west temperature difference across the equatorial Pacific, with an annual cycle (Vallis 1988).

lines: \dot{x} &= b y - c p - c x

name: Wang–Sun system

name: WINDMI magnetosphere model
about: A reduced model of energy flow from the solar wind into Earth's magnetosphere and ionosphere, driven by the solar-wind voltage (Smith, Thiffeault & Horton 2000).

name: Yu–Wang system
about: A chaotic flow with an exponential nonlinearity, realized as a temperature-compensation circuit with an operational amplifier (Yu & Wang 2012).

name: Yu–Wang system 2
about: A second variant of the Yu–Wang system, an alternative temperature-compensation circuit (Yu & Wang 2012).

name: Zhou–Chen system

name: Lorenz system
about: Lorenz's three-mode model of convection in a fluid layer heated from below, the original strange attractor, with its butterfly-shaped double lobe (Lorenz 1963).

name: Lorenz system
about: Lorenz's three-mode model of convection in a fluid layer heated from below, the original strange attractor, with its butterfly-shaped double lobe (Lorenz 1963).

eqs.note: x observed (ρ = 130: strongly chaotic, far above the classic ρ = 28).

name: Chen system
about: A Lorenz-like system found by chaos anti-control (feedback designed to make a system chaotic), whose double-scroll attractor is not equivalent to Lorenz's (Chen & Ueta 1999).

name: Rössler funnel
about: The Rössler system in its funnel regime (a = 0.3, c = 14), where orbits make several small turns between large excursions (Rössler 1976).

name: Chua circuit
about: An electronic circuit of two capacitors, an inductor and a nonlinear negative resistor (Chua's diode), with the famous double-scroll attractor (Matsumoto 1984).

name: Forced Duffing oscillator
about: A damped particle in a double-well potential, shaken periodically so that it hops chaotically between the wells (Duffing 1918; Ueda 1979).

name: Driven pendulum
about: A damped pendulum driven by a periodic torque, which swings and tumbles over the top chaotically.

eqs.note: sin θ observed (θ is unbounded when the pendulum rotates).

name: Double pendulum
about: Two pendulums hung end to end, without friction: a conservative Hamiltonian system that is chaotic at high enough energy.

eqs.note: sin θ₁ observed (equal masses and lengths, g = 1).

name: Lorenz-84 system
about: Lorenz's low-order model of the general circulation of the atmosphere: a westerly jet exchanging energy with traveling eddies (Lorenz 1984).

name: Blasius system
about: A food chain of vegetation, herbivores and predators whose population peaks vary chaotically while their timing stays regular, as in the Canadian lynx cycle (Blasius, Huppert & Stone 1999).
